task.title: Overlap per-tree mount, search and unmount with a small bounded pool
task.problem: After BSG-012 the many-tree content search is serial: ~4.5 ms mount, ~5 ms rg and ~2 ms release per tree (300 trees: 3.5 s of a 5.1 s wall). A prototype pool of 4 workers cut that stage to 0.99 s on 4 CPUs. On freedesktop-sdk sdk.bst (468 trees, 4 CPUs) a no-match content scan spends 282 s in one rg at a time; releases cost 13 s (28 ms per tree after a full read, versus 8 ms to mount).
task.proposal: Run mount+rg (spooling rg output to a temporary file) for up to N trees concurrently, emit completed trees in input order from the main thread, and release each tree after emission. Default N to min(4, CPUs); keep N=1 equivalent to current behaviour. Release trees off the critical path so unmount overlaps the next search.
acceptance: Output order and content are identical to serial mode for every scenario in scripts/bench_source_grep.py.
Active owned mounts and rg processes never exceed the configured bound; --stats reports the observed peak.
Interrupt, closed pipe and per-tree mount/search errors clean up every worker's mount and process.
Benchmark shows the many-tree wall-time gain without regressing single-tree scenarios or memory beyond the spooled output.
evidence: Prototype measurement recorded in BSG-010 evidence.
